full_judgment:
5. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff appellants has urged the ground of special onus on defendants. It, however, requires to be seen how far this contention is sustainable. It is to be observed that the question of special onus with regard to transaction entered into with a pardanashin lady has been settled by a long string of Privy Council decisions. What is now required is to see whether the exposition of law has rightly been made in Ayani Dasi's case 12 D.L.R 603 or it requires reconsideration and restatement, in view of the Privy Council decisions in a number of cases, namely, Nawab Sikander Begum vs Zulfikar Wali Khan A.I.R. 1938 (P. C.) 38; Faridun Nesa vs. Mukhtar Ahmed 30 P.C. No, 337; Sunitibala Devi vs. Dhara Sundari Debi A,I.C. 19 9 (P.0 ) 21; Lala Kundan Lol vs. Mt. Musharrofi Begum A,I.R. 1931 (P. C.) 207; Ramanamma vs. Virunna A. I. R. 1931 (P. C). 100; Musammat Kamawati rs. Kunwar Digbijoi Singh 26 C.W.N. 490 (P.C,); and Bank of Khulna vs. Joti Prokash Mitra 45 C.W.N. 25). It is to be further examined whether the Ayani Dasi's case is applicable to the facts of this case. 

 10. The earliest case is that of Tacoor Deen Tewary vs. Nawab Syed Ali Hossain Khan 1 I.A. 192. it was held by the Privy Council that where a pardanashin lady, lying apart from her relations and natural advisers, makes a deed in favour of a person who has, on some occasions, acted as her man of business, the strongest proof ought to be given by him that the transaction was a real and bonafide one, and was fully understood by the lady whose property is dealt with. It was further observed that in a suit for setting aside deeds some evidence ought to be given by the plaintiff in order to impeach such deeds and is not entitled, merely on the proof of heir ship, to throw on the defendant the burden of showing a better title. It was a suit by a plaintiff in whose favour the lady executed a sale deed which he sought to enforce against the heirs of the lady. It is to be observed that the lady also challenged the document as fraudulent and fabricated and in that context the observation set out above was made by the Privy Council. 

 12. The next decision is in the case of Mirza Sajjad Husain vs Nawab Wazir Ali Khan 39 I.A. 156. Here the suit was brought by the plaintiffs praying for declaration that all the property comprised was a waqf and the plaintiffs were trustees under the deed and claimed for possession and there it appeared that the conveyance was made by a pardanashin woman under which the plaintiff's claimed to be trustees. It was held that the onus was, upon them to show that the transaction had been explained to the pardanashin lady and that she understood it. It was observed that the onus of proof has not been discharged by the plaintiff-appellants and the Privy Council in that view dismissed the appeal. An observation was made in this case following the authority of Tacoor Deen Tewary vs, Nawab Syed Ali Hossain Khan 1 I.A. 192 and Shambati Koeri vs. Argo Bibi 29 I.A 131, stating that it is well-known rule of the Privy Council that in case of the deeds and powers executed by pardanashin ladies, it is a prerequisite that those who rely upon them should satisfy the Court that they have been explained to and understood by those who executed them.
